stances_toward.note: Member and co-founder, graded partner: BRICS has no defence clause and Brazil uses it as a reform vehicle and a stage, not as a bloc to which it commits its market. Brazil chaired the group in 2025 (Rio summit, 6-7 July 2025; Xi sent his premier, Putin joined online), and Trump threatened an extra 10% tariff on states aligning with 'anti-American policies' within hours of the joint statement. In October 2024 Brazil declined the Belt and Road, and the New Delhi declaration of September 2026 (India chairing) dropped Ukraine. Stable: it neither commits nor leaves. Bond none.

stances_toward.note: Partner and the forum Beijing uses as its frame for the non-Western order: Xi at New Delhi (12-13 Sep 2026), where the declaration dropped Ukraine altogether and the Xi-Modi bilateral reset the border talks; the New Development Bank and the yuan as the instruments; Egypt, the UAE and Iran among the members since 2024. Beijing wants the grouping as a vote and a market, not as a bloc with obligations - India and Brazil both declined the Belt and Road. Bond - affinity: the shared reading of the order.

stances_toward.note: Partner: a BRICS member, and the forum in which Pretoria frames its trade with China (with FOCAC). The 2010 accession date is not in the sources retrieved and must be verified before publication. Trend warming: the bloc is the stage on which South Africa claims a Global South voice after the 2025 G20. Bond none: membership is interest. Added 2026-10-16: Ramaphosa attended the 18th summit in New Delhi on 12-13 September 2026 (theme set by India; South Africa's agenda was intra-BRICS trade, industrialisation and African infrastructure under the AfCFTA, per the Presidency), and Trump's July 2025 threat of an extra 10% tariff on countries aligned with BRICS's 'anti-American policies' is the cost side of the same membership (see the BRICS-and-the-rand paradox in the card).
